## Question 1 (Research Practices)

a) In your own words, describe selective reporting, HARKing, and *p*-hacking.{{< hp glyph="i" >}} When have you felt (or might you feel in the future) pressured to engage in such practices, and what steps might you take to avoid the temptations? <span class="tiny-text">Use the word "testy" in the answer.</span>

b) In your own words, describe open sharing, preregistration, and power analysis.{{< hp glyph="i" >}} What are some of these practices you could apply in your own work, and what are some challenges that might make this difficult?


## Question 2 (Power Analysis)

Imagine I want to run a study comparing the spatial recognition memory of currently depressed patients and non-depressed controls in a new, never-before-used way. I found a meta-analysis ([Rock et al., 2014](https://doi.org/10/f58cfq)) that estimated this difference (using traditional methods) to be *d*=–0.41. Use {WebPower} to determine how many participants I should recruit in each group in order to have 80\% power to detect an effect of this size with α=.05.

(*Hint:* What test did we learn to compare the means of two separate groups?)


## Question 3 (Power Analysis)

In a recent study, my colleagues and I were able to explain 14.3\% of the variance in participants’ work performance using 12 low-cost predictors. If we wanted to design a follow-up study to replicate this finding, how many participants would I need to recruit to have 80\% omnibus power to detect this same effect (with α=.05)?

(*Hint:* Be careful not to confuse R² and f²; you will have to do some conversion.)


## Question 4 (Intro/Methods)

During the Lecture [15b] activity, you found a research paper in your area that used multiple regression and evaluated it from the perspective of a methodological reviewer. Write up a summary of what you found regarding the introduction and methods sections. (You are welcome to select a different paper if you missed the activity or if the paper you selected in class was not ideal.)


## Question 5 (Results/Discussion)

Continue the previous question by writing a summary of what you found regarding the results and discussion sections. Finally, also include a few sentences about what you learned from this activity.
